scope: verify the reliableCommands offset against the native source and find why the key never advances

client_t_layout.reliableCommands: client_t + 0xa50 (2640), 128 entries of {int cmdTime; int cmdType; char command[1024]}

source_findings.decode_function: SV_Netchan_Decode: command = reliableCommands[reliableAcknowledge & 127].command; if 2697 archives active it is mapped through CODOL2697_ReliableKeyCommand (only 'J '/'K ' prefixes become "!"); CODOL_Xor(data, len, key, command, 1024) with key = challenge ^ (byte)serverId ^ messageAcknowledge
source_findings.xor_function: CODOL_Xor advances the byte key with command[j++] << (i & 1) and skips a NUL back to index 0, which matches forge_client_ack.encode

experiment.result: command_len is still 0 because reliableAcknowledge is 0 and reliableCommands[0] is genuinely empty; the decoder would also use the empty command, so the key stays at its initial value in both directions

decisive_clue.meaning: the dedrun's client->serverId is 1 while forge_client_ack hard-coded server_id 0
decisive_clue.impact: key = challenge ^ (byte)serverId ^ messageAcknowledge differs by 1 in the low byte for every byte of the packet, so the dedrun's decoder produces garbage and discards the ack
decisive_clue.fix: ring_bridge now takes --forge-server-id (default 1) and passes it into encode()

next: re-run one session with the default server id 1 and watch whether out stops growing / reliableAcknowledge advances
if it still fails, try server id 0 and 1 side by side and log which one the dedrun accepts
also log the dedrun's raw serverId field once the offset is known, so the value no longer depends on the log line
